Living Well / Free resources

Relationships, memory & listening

A useful way in

Choose one place to begin.

Questions and practical resources for listening carefully, preserving a story, and making participation easier.

A useful resource can make it easier to begin a conversation or keep an agreed memory accessible. It cannot decide what another person wants to share. Start with an invitation, listen to the answer, and choose an activity that respects everyone involved.

Start with: A question for a real conversation. Choose one question from Great Questions for Anyone and ask whether the person would enjoy discussing it.

Visual assistance and human help

Be My Eyes

A concrete example of technology supporting access: blind and low-vision users can seek visual assistance from people and AI. There is also a volunteering route.

Access: Free personal-use app with setup/sign-in. Commercial offerings and optional hardware are separate.

Keep the context

Take what is useful, thoughtfully.

Recording, uploading, editing, and publishing are separate decisions. Ask about each relevant use rather than assuming that a friendly conversation grants blanket permission. Some people will prefer a private, unrecorded exchange. For technology-supported assistance, follow the provider’s safety and privacy guidance and the preferences of the person receiving help.

Selections are based on public source review, not a claim that Nolan uses every resource or belongs to the organizations listed.
